title: D4 X-only flux-threshold validation
question: Do matched O0, O2, and D4-BP flux-recovery curves exhibit a reproducible finite-size crossing on the real D4 channel, and is any BP advantage robust to nonconvergence and scoring audits?
gates: Replay all R6U BP zero-failure rows from serialized physical error, public observation, and correction provenance; independently verify Boolean-union scorer and no decoder truth leakage.
Repeat each R6U cell with both final-iterate and converged-only accounting; register a damping/iteration sensitivity only if nonconvergence changes policy ordering.

After the integrity gate, sample matched X-only D4 trajectories at L=5,7,9,11,13 over the preregistered p_X grid 0.14,0.16,...,0.30. Stage 1 has 1000 attempted histories per cell; any Stage 2 expansion is a predeclared 1000-history increment up to 5000, restricted to p/size pairs selected by the Stage 1 crossing-precision rule.

Report binomial intervals, paired policy contrasts, adjacent-size LER differences, terminal-winding rate, and BP convergence. A crossing is finite-size evidence only; threshold promotion requires stable multi-size behavior and a completed scoring gate.

scan_design.stage_2_selection_rule: For a policy and adjacent size pair, allocate the next matched 1000-history increment only to grid p_X values whose 90% independent-size risk-difference interval contains zero, plus their immediately adjacent grid points. Apply the same selected trajectories to O0, O2, and BP. Stop a policy/pair after no selected grid point remains, the per-cell cap is reached, or the BP convergence-sensitivity gate changes the policy ordering.

launch_guard.reason: The R6U zero-failure BP signal must be provenance- and scorer-audited before any large threshold allocation.

claim_boundary: This studies the X-only first-stage D4 flux-decoding threshold proxy, not full D4 two-stage fault tolerance or Lab 003 equivalence.
